root.label: Iostreams
root.note: Formatting streams over stream buffers, with a state word and persistent formatting state.

children.label: Layers
children.note: Streams format and track state; stream buffers move characters.

children.label: basic_ios and streambuf
children.note: basic_ios holds a pointer to a streambuf that does the actual buffering and transport.

children.label: Buffer types
children.note: filebuf, stringbuf, spanbuf and syncbuf are the standard stream buffers.

children.label: Locale per stream
children.note: Each stream copies the global locale at construction and uses it for number formatting.

children.label: State bits
children.note: A state word records what went wrong with the last operation.

children.label: failbit
children.note: The operation did not succeed; it makes the stream convert to false.

children.label: eofbit
children.note: A read hit the end of input; it can be set even when the read succeeded.

children.label: badbit
children.note: The stream buffer lost integrity; a parse error never sets it.

children.label: while (in >> x)
children.note: Put the extraction in the condition; looping on eof() repeats the last value.

children.label: clear()
children.note: A failed stream ignores operations until clear(); str() does not reset the bits.

children.label: Input styles
children.note: Formatted and unformatted input behave differently around whitespace.

children.label: Formatted operator>>
children.note: Skips leading whitespace and parses a value; failure stores 0 for numbers.

children.label: Unformatted functions
children.note: get, getline, read, ignore and peek take characters as they are.

children.label: Newline after >>
children.note: operator>> leaves the newline, so a following getline returns an empty line.

children.label: Output formatting
children.note: Manipulators change formatting state, mostly permanently.

children.label: Sticky manipulators
children.note: hex, fixed, setfill, setprecision and alignment persist until changed.

children.label: setw is one-shot
children.note: Width applies to the next formatted output only and never truncates.

children.label: endl versus newline
children.note: endl writes a newline and flushes; '\n' does not flush.

children.label: Performance and threads
children.note: Standard streams are synchronized with C stdio by default.

children.label: sync_with_stdio(false)
children.note: Call before any I/O; it drops C stdio mixing and the concurrent-access guarantee.

children.label: cin.tie(nullptr)
children.note: Stops cout being flushed before every cin read.

children.label: osyncstream
children.note: C++20 stream that emits its buffered text to the target as one unit.

children.label: Streams over memory and files
children.note: Memory and file streams share the stream interface.

children.label: String streams
children.note: str() returns a copy and does not clear the state bits.

children.label: spanstream (C++23)
children.note: Streams over a caller-owned buffer with no allocation; span() shows the written part.

children.label: File open modes
children.note: in|out requires an existing file and keeps content; out truncates; app appends.

children.label: Exceptions mask
children.note: exceptions(failbit) throws ios_base::failure, including at the end of a read loop.
